header.title: Bot settings
header.description: Global settings for {guild}. Settings specific to each module (Tickets, Whitelist, etc.) live inside the module itself.

global.botLocaleHint: Language of the bot's messages, buttons and replies in this server. Command names show in each person's Discord language. Texts you wrote (welcome messages, panels, forms) don't change.
global.logsChannelHint: Channel that receives the bot's general logs, or 'None' to turn them off.
global.notifyDmHint: Sends the member a DM when their subscription is activated, renewed, fails or expires, and when they win a giveaway. In DMs the bot shows up with the app's global identity; the embed shows the server name and icon for context. Turn it off if you'd rather notify only in the public channel.

invite.statusMissing: {count, plural, one {# permission missing} other {# permissions missing}}
invite.title: Reinvite bot
invite.description: Updates the bot's permissions on Discord. Useful after enabling new modules or upgrading your plan.
invite.ctaHint: Opens Discord in a new tab with the permissions already selected.

BanMembers.label: Ban members
BanMembers.description: Ban from the panel or by command.

ModerateMembers.label: Mute (timeout)
ModerateMembers.description: Mute for up to 28 days, no role needed.

ManageMessages.label: Manage messages
ManageMessages.description: Clear messages, auto moderation and pinning notices.

ViewAuditLog.label: Audit log
ViewAuditLog.description: See bans and edits made directly on Discord.

GuildMembers.label: Server members
GuildMembers.description: Automatic roles, welcomes and join logs.

MessageContent.label: Message content
MessageContent.description: Logs of deleted and edited messages, with their text.

GuildModeration.label: Server moderation
GuildModeration.description: Notice bans made directly on Discord.

GuildVoiceStates.label: Voice states
GuildVoiceStates.description: Logs of joining and leaving voice channels.

news.saveError: Failed to save the announcement settings.
news.title: Bot news
news.description: When a new module, command or feature ships, the bot announces it on your server.
news.fallbackHint: By default, in your logs channel.
news.noTargetHint: You don't have a logs channel or a chosen channel yet, so nothing will be sent.
news.autoDisabled: The announcement was turned off automatically: {reason} Fix it and turn it back on.

tickets.title: Ticket settings
tickets.description: Opening defaults, types, behavior and support panels. Each section saves separately.
tickets.integerRange: Use a whole number between 0 and {max}.

defaults.panelDescription: Need help? Click the button below to open a ticket. A staff member will reply as soon as possible.
defaults.selectPlaceholder: Choose the reason for your ticket
defaults.outOfHoursMessage: We're outside support hours. Feel free to describe your question, we'll reply as soon as we're back.

defaultsSection.title: Defaults
defaultsSection.description: Category and role used when someone opens a ticket, and the channel that keeps the history.
defaultsSection.noCategories: No categories found on the server.
defaultsSection.staffRoleNone: None, only the creator sees the ticket
defaultsSection.logChannelNone: None, history stays in the panel only
defaultsSection.logChannelHint: When a ticket closes, the bot posts here who opened it, who handled it, how long it lasted and a link to the full history. Make this channel visible to staff only.

behavior.title: Ticket behavior
behavior.description: Limits and automations that control the ticket lifecycle.
behavior.maxOpenHint: How many tickets each user can have open at the same time. 0 = unlimited.
behavior.autoCloseHint: Close tickets with no new message after N hours. 0 = disabled.
behavior.autoClaimHint: The first staff member to reply to the ticket takes it over automatically; this applies to messages in the channel, {command} and replies from the panel. Whoever opened the ticket never claims their own ticket, and anonymous replies don't claim either.
behavior.nudgeHint: Button on the ticket panel that DMs the other side: staff nudges whoever opened it, and whoever opened it nudges whoever took it over. Since it becomes a DM, each side has a minimum wait between one nudge and the next {sameTicket}. Set {zero} to disable that side; both at 0 hide the button.
behavior.nudgeStaffHint: Applies to the whole staff, not per member.
behavior.nudgeMemberHint: Only works after someone takes over the ticket.
behavior.conflictingType: The "{label}" type has a limit of {limit}. Adjust it in "Ticket types" before lowering the global limit.

types.title: Ticket types
types.description: Up to {max} types. Each type becomes a button (or a dropdown option) on the panel. Empty = a single generic "Open ticket" button.
types.label: Label
types.labelInvalid: Label must be between 2 and 50 characters.
types.descriptionHintSelect: Shows under the name in the panel's dropdown.
types.descriptionHintButtons: Only shows on "dropdown" style panels· with buttons, Discord doesn't show descriptions.
types.welcomePlaceholder: Posted in the channel on open. E.g. Describe your problem with screenshots.
types.maxOpen: Limit open tickets of this type
types.maxOpenHint: How many tickets of this type each user can have open at the same time. Off = only the global limit applies. Can never exceed the global limit.
types.maxOpenHintWithGlobal: How many tickets of this type each user can have open at the same time. Off = only the global limit applies. Can never exceed the global limit ({global}).
types.formHint: Questions the user answers when opening this type. Empty = only asks for the subject.
types.fieldLabelInvalid: The question must be between 1 and 45 characters.
types.keyInvalid: Key must be kebab-case (lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens) with 2 to 40 characters.
types.keyDuplicated: This key is already used by another type.
types.emptyDescription: Without types, the panel shows a single "Open ticket" button. Add types to split support (e.g. Support, Report, Question).
types.invalid: Some types have invalid fields or duplicate keys.
types.blockedByGlobal: Save "Ticket behavior" first, the saved global limit is still lower than some type's limit.

canned.title: Canned responses
canned.description: Default replies staff posts in the channel with {command}; autocomplete filters by name.
canned.contentPlaceholder: Content posted in the channel (supports mentions, markdown and Unicode emojis).
canned.invalid: Every response needs a name and content.

blacklist.title: Blacklist
blacklist.description: Blocks specific users from opening tickets. Enter the Discord ID (right-click the user with developer mode on). Limit: {max}.

hours.title: Support hours
hours.description: Window when staff is available. Outside it the ticket opens normally, it just gets a notice in the channel to set expectations.
hours.messagePlaceholder: E.g. We're outside support hours. We'll reply as soon as possible.
hours.off: Off, tickets are handled without a time window.

panels.title: Ticket panels
panels.description: Multiple panels (e.g. support and billing), each with its own channel, design, style and subset of types. On Discord, {command} picks which one to post.
panels.style: How the user picks the type
panels.styleButtonsHint: One button per type, 5 per row. Opens in 1 click.
panels.styleSelectHint: A single list with a description for each type. Takes less space.
panels.noTypesWarning: With no types configured, both styles post the same single "Open ticket" button.
panels.selectMax: The dropdown shows at most 25 types.
panels.selectTextHint: Empty = "{placeholder}". Each option's description comes from the type's "Description" field.
panels.shownTypesHint: Leave empty to show all types.
panels.contentHintSelect: Build it with blocks. The types dropdown is added automatically.
panels.contentHintButtons: Build it with blocks. The type buttons are added automatically.
panels.saveTypesFirst: Save the types before publishing, the panel uses the saved types.
panels.alreadyPublished: Already published, republishing deletes the previous one.

always.label: Always
always.hint: Every application goes to the queue. The answer-key score shows on the card but doesn't decide.

passingOnly.label: Only those who pass the answer key
passingOnly.hint: Wrong answers are rejected right away. Those who pass go to the queue so staff can read the answers.

never.label: Never
never.hint: The score approves and rejects on its own. With no answer-key question, everything goes to the queue.

cooldown.daysHours: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} and {rest}h

whitelist.windowProblem: The window closes before it opens, nobody would be able to apply.

fieldProblem.key: Question {number} ("{title}"): the internal code has an invalid character.
fieldProblem.key-dup: Question {number} ("{title}"): the internal code repeats another question's.
fieldProblem.label: Question {number} ("{title}"): the title must be between 2 and 45 characters.
fieldProblem.content: Question {number} ("{title}"): the text block is empty.
fieldProblem.options-min: Question {number} ("{title}") needs options to choose from.
fieldProblem.option-empty: Question {number} ("{title}") has an option without text.
fieldProblem.option-dup: Question {number} ("{title}") has two options with the same value.
fieldProblem.minValues: Question {number} ("{title}"): the minimum number of choices doesn't fit the number of options.
fieldProblem.maxValues: Question {number} ("{title}"): the maximum number of choices doesn't fit the number of options.
fieldProblem.values-range: Question {number} ("{title}"): the minimum number of choices is greater than the maximum.
fieldProblem.min: Question {number} ("{title}"): the minimum length is invalid.
fieldProblem.max: Question {number} ("{title}"): the maximum length is invalid.
fieldProblem.range: Question {number} ("{title}"): the minimum length is greater than the maximum.

whitelist.overPlanProblem: your plan allows up to {limit} questions per form. Remove the extra ones.
whitelist.validateList: Check the form fields, some entries are invalid or duplicated.
whitelist.validateOverPlan: Your plan allows up to {limit} questions per form. Remove the extra ones to save.

approval.title: When to ask for staff approval
approval.description: Applies to the form. The "Use code" button bypasses this, it's the shortcut for people already cleared some other way.
approval.noGrading: No question has a preset answer, so there's no score to decide anything: for now, everything keeps going to the staff queue.

panel.title: Panel, review and role
panel.description: Where the apply button lives, where staff reviews, and the role given on approval.
panel.noQuestions: The form has no questions. Add the questions and save before posting the panel.
panel.reviewChannelHint: Applications arrive here for staff to approve or reject. Make this channel visible to staff only.
panel.noReviewChannel: Without a review channel, each application shows up in the channel where the person clicked Apply, with the answers visible to everyone.
panel.approvedRoleHint: Role the bot will add to the user after approval.
panel.appearanceHint: What shows above the apply button. After changing it, save and click Post again, above.

form.title: Form
form.description: A single form, with whatever question types you want: text box, number, single choice, multiple choice and consent. Any choice question can have a preset answer, and that's what becomes the score.
form.keyHint: The {key} is filled in automatically from the question text; edit it if you want your own name. Once saved it stops following the text, since answers are stored under it, and renaming it detaches the question from earlier applications.
form.paginated: Beyond that the applicant answers in pages; your plan allows {limit}, in up to {screens} screens.
form.notPaginated: Your plan allows {limit}; Pro unlocks up to {ceiling}, answered in up to 3 screens.
form.fieldCount: {count}/{limit} fields · {pages, plural, one {one screen} other {# screens}}
form.overPlan: This form has {count} fields and the plan allows {limit}. Remove {excess} to be able to save.
form.noQuestionsHint: With no questions at all, whoever clicks {apply} fills in a single field, the name, and the request goes to the queue. This is the setup for those who screen outside Discord.
form.passSummary: {count, plural, one {# question is graded} other {# questions are graded}}: anyone who gets {needed} or more right passes.
form.passNever: Pass, approved right away; fail, rejected right away.
form.passPassingOnly: Those who don't pass are rejected right away; those who pass go to the queue.
form.passAlways: The score only shows on the card, staff decides.
form.archivedHint: These came from the other mode's form, from when the whitelist had separate modes. Nobody answers these questions today:
form.archivedAction: Bring them into the form or discard them.
form.archivedAtLimit: The form is already at the plan limit ({limit}). Remove a question to make room.

draw.title: Draw and time limit
draw.description: Against cheating: what gets passed around on Discord is "the third one is C". Each option here breaks a piece of that sentence.
draw.perForm: How many questions each applicant answers
draw.perFormSome: Each applicant answers {perForm} of the {total} questions.
draw.pinnedAlways: {count, plural, one {The pinned one always shows up} other {The # pinned ones always show up}}; the other {drawn} are drawn at random.
draw.drawnHint: Drawn at random, two applicants almost never get the same test.
draw.perFormAll: {zero} = all {total}. Set a lower number to turn the form into a question bank.
draw.pinnedFloor: You pinned {count} questions, and pinned ones always show up, so the minimum per form is {count}. Unpin some to ask for fewer.
draw.gradeVaries: The score is calculated only from the answer-key questions that get drawn, so it can vary from applicant to applicant.
draw.shuffleQuestionsHint: Each applicant gets the questions in a random order.
draw.shufflePinned: {count, plural, one {The pinned one stays at the start.} other {The pinned ones stay at the start.}}
draw.shuffleTextBlocks: Text blocks stay where you put them.
draw.shufflePages: Questions change screens, not just positions.
draw.shuffleOptionsHint: The option order changes on every screen. That's what makes "it's choice B" worthless; the answer is stored by option, not by position.
draw.noTimeLimit: No time limit, the applicant takes as long as they want.
draw.timeLimitHint: Counts from the click on "Apply" until submission. If time runs out, they start over from scratch, with newly drawn questions.
draw.timeCheckPaged: Discord doesn't let the bot close a form that's already open, so the time is checked on each submitted screen (and the applicant sees how much is left between them).
draw.timeCheck: Discord doesn't let the bot close a form that's already open, so the time is checked on each submitted screen.

retry.title: Try again
retry.description: Anyone already {approved} never retakes the whitelist. Anyone {rejected} waits the time below.
retry.cooldownHint: {duration}. Also applies to automatic test rejections.
retry.windowHint: Outside the period, the "Apply" button replies that it's closed. Leave empty to always accept. The "Use code" button keeps working, it exists precisely to bypass the whitelist.

announcements.title: Public announcements
announcements.description: Optional channels where the bot announces each decision. Without a channel, nothing is posted. Use {user}, {character}, {score}, {reason} and {reviewer} in the text.

codes.title: Access codes
codes.description: With this on, the panel gets a "Use code" button next to "Apply". Anyone with a valid code gets in directly, skipping the queue.
codes.immediate: The codes below take effect immediately, they don't depend on this screen's save button.

whitelistPanel.dirty: Save your changes before posting, otherwise the panel goes out without them.
whitelistPanel.postedReplaced: Panel posted. The old one was deleted.
whitelistPanel.hint: Where the "Apply" button everyone sees lives.
whitelistPanel.currentChannel: The panel is currently in {channel}. Posting again deletes the old one.

whitelistCodes.created: {count, plural, one {Code created} other {# codes created}}
whitelistCodes.manualInvalid: Use {min} to {max} characters, only letters, numbers and hyphens.

whitelistFields.pinnedTitle: Pinned: opens the form and stays out of the draw
whitelistFields.pinTitle: Pin to the start of the form
whitelistFields.question: Question
whitelistFields.labelInvalid: Use 2 to {max} characters, that's Discord's limit.
whitelistFields.keyTitle: Answer identifier. Filled in from the question, edit it to set your own.
whitelistFields.contentHint: It's not a question and gets no answer, but it takes one of the {size} slots on the screen.
whitelistFields.checkboxHint: Discord has no "required" for a single checkbox. When marked as required, it's enforced on submit: the applicant gets the warning after submitting, not before.
whitelistFields.valueHint: The {value} is what gets stored in the answer; renaming the text doesn't break applications already submitted.
whitelistFields.valueHintGrading: Mark the answer that scores on the left.
whitelistFields.exactly: Scores only if they check {exactly} these {count} options, there's no partial credit.
whitelistFields.radioMin: Single choice with visible options needs at least 2 options.
whitelistFields.optionEmpty: Every option needs text and a value.
whitelistFields.optionDup: Some options have the same value.
whitelistFields.gradedToggle: Scores if the person checks it
whitelistFields.writeQuestion: Write the question, the key is filled in from it.
whitelistFields.keyInvalid: Key must be kebab-case (lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens) with 2 to 40 characters.
whitelistFields.keyDup: This key is already used by another field.
whitelistFields.range: Min can't be greater than Max.
whitelistFields.valuesRange: Min. choices can't be greater than the maximum.
whitelistFields.valuesFit: The choice limits must fit the number of options.
